steps.message:
Build a 9-slide, 16:9 PowerPoint presentation titled "Global CO₂ Emissions: Who Emits, How Much, and What's Changing" for policy analysts, climate negotiators, and sustainability researchers. The tone should be data-forward, analytical, and accessible.

The deck opens with a title slide establishing scope (fossil fuels & industry, 1750–2024) and data attribution (Global Carbon Budget 2025 via Our World in Data). It then traces the narrative arc from historical emission growth, through the dramatic shift in regional shares, to today's country-level dominance by China — before pivoting to per capita inequalities that reframe responsibility. The final slides examine 2024 trends, the role of energy mix in driving differences, and close with key takeaways on shared but unequal responsibility.

For the "Global CO₂ Emissions Grew from 6 Bt in 1950 to Over 35 Bt Today" slide, use an area or line chart showing the long-run trajectory with annotated inflection points. For the "Per Capita Emissions Range from 0.1 t in Chad to ~14 t in the US and Canada" slide, use a horizontal bar chart highlighting the 150x gap between the lowest and highest emitting nations. Where charts are described in other slides (stacked area, treemap, multi-line, diverging bar, comparative bar), represent them visually or as clearly labeled placeholder chart descriptions.

Do not fabricate data not found in source_brief.md. All figures, percentages, and country-level values must come directly from the provided slide specifications.


## Data Sources

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

1	# Global CO₂ Emissions: Who Emits, How Much, and What's Changing
2	
3	## Source
4	https://ourworldindata.org/co2-emissions — Data from the Global Carbon Budget (2025). Authors: Hannah Ritchie and Max Roser.
5	
6	## Global Emission Trajectory
7	
8	Global CO₂ emissions from fossil fuels and industry have grown dramatically since the Industrial Revolution. Before industrialization, emissions were negligible. By 1950, the world emitted roughly 6 billion tonnes (Bt) of CO₂ per year. By 1990, this had nearly quadrupled to over 20 Bt. Today, global emissions exceed 35 Bt annually. While growth has slowed in recent years, emissions have not yet peaked.
9	
10	![Global CO₂ emissions over time](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
11	
12	Emissions from land-use change have declined slightly in recent years, but fossil fuel emissions continue to dominate the total.
13	
14	## Regional and Country Shares
15	
16	The distribution of emissions has shifted profoundly over time. In 1900, Europe and the United States accounted for more than 90% of global CO₂ emissions. By 1950, they still represented over 85%. Today, they account for less than one-third. Asia — led by China — now dominates, producing roughly half of global emissions.
17	
18	![Share of global CO₂ emissions by country](./assets/figure_6.jpg)
19	
20	| Country / Region | Approx. Share of Global CO₂ (2024) | Trend |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| China | ~31% | Rising, growth slowing |
23	| United States | ~13% | Declining |
24	| India | ~8% | Rising |
25	| European Union (27) | ~6% | Declining |
26	| Russia | ~5% | Roughly stable |
27	| Africa (total) | ~3–4% | Slowly rising |
28	| South America (total) | ~3–4% | Roughly stable |
29	| Int'l aviation & shipping | ~3% | Rising |
30	
31	Africa and South America each account for only 3–4% of global emissions — comparable to international aviation and shipping combined.
32	
33	## Per Capita Emissions and Inequality
34	
35	Per capita CO₂ emissions reveal stark global inequalities. The world's largest per capita emitters are major oil-producing nations with small populations (Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait). Among large, populous countries, the United States, Australia, and Canada have per capita emissions roughly three times the global average.
36	
37	![Per capita CO₂ emissions over time](./assets/figure_8.jpg)
38	
39	| Country | Per Capita CO₂ (approx. 2024) |
40	|---|---|
41	| United States | ~14 t |
42	| Canada | ~14 t |
43	| China | ~9 t |
44	| South Africa | ~7 t |
45	| European Union (27) | ~6 t |
46	| World average | ~4.5 t |
47	| United Kingdom | ~4 t |
48	| India | ~2 t |
49	| Kenya | ~0.4 t |
50	| Chad / Niger | ~0.1 t |
51	
52	The gap is enormous: the average American or Australian emits in under two days what the average person in Mali or Niger emits in an entire year — a roughly 150x difference.
53	
54	Even among wealthy nations, per capita emissions vary significantly. France, the UK, and Portugal have much lower per capita emissions than Germany, the Netherlands, or the US, largely because a higher share of their electricity comes from nuclear and renewable sources rather than fossil fuels.
55

# Global CO₂ Emissions: Who Emits, How Much, and What's Changing

## Source
https://ourworldindata.org/co2-emissions — Data from the Global Carbon Budget (2025). Authors: Hannah Ritchie and Max Roser.

## Global Emission Trajectory

Global CO₂ emissions from fossil fuels and industry have grown dramatically since the Industrial Revolution. Before industrialization, emissions were negligible. By 1950, the world emitted roughly 6 billion tonnes (Bt) of CO₂ per year. By 1990, this had nearly quadrupled to over 20 Bt. Today, global emissions exceed 35 Bt annually. While growth has slowed in recent years, emissions have not yet peaked.

![Global CO₂ emissions over time](./assets/figure_2.jpg)

Emissions from land-use change have declined slightly in recent years, but fossil fuel emissions continue to dominate the total.

## Regional and Country Shares

The distribution of emissions has shifted profoundly over time. In 1900, Europe and the United States accounted for more than 90% of global CO₂ emissions. By 1950, they still represented over 85%. Today, they account for less than one-third. Asia — led by China — now dominates, producing roughly half of global emissions.

![Share of global CO₂ emissions by country](./assets/figure_6.jpg)

| Country / Region | Approx. Share of Global CO₂ (2024) | Trend |
|---|---|---|
| China | ~31% | Rising, growth slowing |
| United States | ~13% | Declining |
| India | ~8% | Rising |
| European Union (27) | ~6% | Declining |
| Russia | ~5% | Roughly stable |
| Africa (total) | ~3–4% | Slowly rising |
| South America (total) | ~3–4% | Roughly stable |
| Int'l aviation & shipping | ~3% | Rising |

Africa and South America each account for only 3–4% of global emissions — comparable to international aviation and shipping combined.

## Per Capita Emissions and Inequality

Per capita CO₂ emissions reveal stark global inequalities. The world's largest per capita emitters are major oil-producing nations with small populations (Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait). Among large, populous countries, the United States, Australia, and Canada have per capita emissions roughly three times the global average.

![Per capita CO₂ emissions over time](./assets/figure_8.jpg)

| Country | Per Capita CO₂ (approx. 2024) |
|---|---|
| United States | ~14 t |
| Canada | ~14 t |
| China | ~9 t |
| South Africa | ~7 t |
| European Union (27) | ~6 t |
| World average | ~4.5 t |
| United Kingdom | ~4 t |
| India | ~2 t |
| Kenya | ~0.4 t |
| Chad / Niger | ~0.1 t |

The gap is enormous: the average American or Australian emits in under two days what the average person in Mali or Niger emits in an entire year — a roughly 150x difference.

Even among wealthy nations, per capita emissions vary significantly. France, the UK, and Portugal have much lower per capita emissions than Germany, the Netherlands, or the US, largely because a higher share of their electricity comes from nuclear and renewable sources rather than fossil fuels.

## 2024 Annual Change

The map of annual percentage change in CO₂ emissions for 2024 shows a mixed picture. Many Western nations — including the US, much of the EU, and the UK — saw emissions decline (shown in blue). Meanwhile, Russia, parts of Southeast Asia, and several African nations experienced increases (shown in orange and red). Some countries in Central Asia (e.g., Turkmenistan/Uzbekistan region) saw particularly large increases exceeding 10%.

![Annual percentage change in CO₂ emissions, 2024](./assets/figure_5.jpg)

## Key Findings

- **No peak yet**: Global CO₂ emissions from fossil fuels exceed 35 billion tonnes per year and have not yet peaked, despite slowing growth.
- **Dramatic shift in responsibility**: Europe and the US dominated emissions historically (>90% in 1900) but now account for less than one-third; China alone emits over a quarter of the global total.
- **Massive per capita inequality**: A 150x gap exists between the lowest emitters (Sub-Saharan Africa, ~0.1 t/person) and the highest large-country emitters (US/Canada/Australia, ~14–15 t/person).
- **Energy policy matters**: Countries with similar prosperity levels can have very different per capita emissions depending on their energy mix — France and the UK emit far less per capita than Germany or the US.
- **Mixed 2024 signals**: While many developed nations reduced emissions in 2024, increases in parts of Asia, the Middle East, and Africa offset some of these gains.

                title_size=22, sub_size=13, t_offset=Inches(0.52))

    # Stacked area chart
    yrs = list(range(1850, 2025, 5))
    def interp(pts, y):
        xs = sorted(pts.keys())
        for i in range(len(xs)-1):
            if xs[i] <= y <= xs[i+1]:
                t = (y - xs[i]) / (xs[i+1] - xs[i])
                return pts[xs[i]] * (1-t) + pts[xs[i+1]] * t
        if y < xs[0]: return pts[xs[0]]
        return pts[xs[-1]]

    # region shares (approximate, consistent with source data)
    eur_pts  = {1850:55, 1900:50, 1950:35, 1970:28, 1990:18, 2010:12, 2024:8}
    usa_pts  = {1850:10, 1900:28, 1950:40, 1970:32, 1990:22, 2010:16, 2024:13}

    section_tag(slide, "REGIONAL SHIFT")

                "Europe and the US Fell from 90% of Emissions in 1900 to Under One-Third Today",
                "Share of global CO₂ emissions by region  |  1850–2024",
                title_size=22, sub_size=13, t_offset=Inches(0.52))

    # Stacked area chart
    yrs = list(range(1850, 2025, 5))
    def interp(pts, y):
        xs = sorted(pts.keys())
        for i in range(len(xs)-1):
            if xs[i] <= y <= xs[i+1]:
                t = (y - xs[i]) / (xs[i+1] - xs[i])
                return pts[xs[i]] * (1-t) + pts[xs[i+1]] * t
        if y < xs[0]: return pts[xs[0]]
        return pts[xs[-1]]

    # region shares (approximate, consistent with source data)
    eur_pts  = {1850:55, 1900:50, 1950:35, 1970:28, 1990:18, 2010:12, 2024:8}
    usa_pts  = {1850:10, 1900:28, 1950:40, 1970:32, 1990:22, 2010:16, 2024:13}
    chn_pts  = {1850:5,  1900:4,  1950:2,  1970:6,  1990:11, 2010:24, 2024:31}
    ind_pts  = {1850:5,  1900:4,  1950:3,  1970:3,  1990:4,  2010:6,  2024:8}
    oth_pts  = {1850:25, 1900:14, 1950:20, 1970:31, 1990:45, 2010:42, 2024:40}

    eur  = [interp(eur_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    usa  = [interp(usa_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    chn  = [interp(chn_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    ind  = [interp(ind_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    oth  = [interp(oth_pts, y) for y in yrs]

    # Normalize to 100%
    totals = [e+u+c+i+o for e,u,c,i,o in zip(eur,usa,chn,ind,oth)]
    eur  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(eur, totals)]
    usa  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(usa, totals)]
    chn  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(chn, totals)]
    ind  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(ind, totals)]
    oth  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(oth, totals)]

"""

"""
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import matplotlib.ticker as ticker
import numpy as np
import io, os

# ── Color palette ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C_BG        = RGBColor(0x0D, 0x1B, 0x2A)   # dark navy
C_ACCENT    = RGBColor(0x00, 0xB4, 0xD8)   # cyan
C_ACCENT2   = RGBColor(0xEF, 0x6C, 0x00)   # orange
C_ACCENT3   = RGBColor(0x2E, 0xCC, 0x71)   # green
C_LIGHT     = RGBColor(0xE0, 0xE6, 0xEF)   # off-white
C_MID       = RGBColor(0x8A, 0x9B, 0xAB)   # muted blue-grey
C_WHITE     = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
C_TITLE_BG  = RGBColor(0x07, 0x0F, 0x1A)

# matplotlib hex equivalents
M_BG      = '#0D1B2A'
M_ACC     = '#00B4D8'
M_ACC2    = '#EF6C00'
M_ACC3    = '#2ECC71'
M_LIGHT   = '#E0E6EF'
M_MID     = '#8A9BAB'
M_GRID    = '#1E3048'

SLIDE_W = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_H = Inches(7.5)

# ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def new_prs():
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width  = SLIDE_W
    prs.slide_height = SLIDE_H
    return prs

def blank_layout(prs):
    return prs.slide_layouts[6]   # completely blank

def add_slide(prs):
    return prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout(prs))

def fill_slide_bg(slide, color: RGBColor):
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_rect(slide, l, t, w, h, fill_color, alpha=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(1, l, t, w, h)   # MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE=1
    shape.line.fill.background()
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    return shape

def add_textbox(slide, text, l, t, w, h,
                font_size=18, bold=False, color=C_WHITE,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, wrap=True, italic=False):
    txb = slide.shapes.add_textbox(l, t, w, h)
    txb.word_wrap = wrap
    tf = txb.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    return txb

def add_text_para(tf, text, font_size=16, bold=False, color=C_LIGHT,
                  align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, space_before=Pt(4), italic=False):
    from pptx.util import Pt as _Pt
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.alignment = align
    p.space_before = space_before
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size = _Pt(font_size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    return p

def img_to_stream(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight',
                facecolor=M_BG, edgecolor='none')
    buf.seek(0)
    return buf

def add_chart_img(slide, fig, l, t, w, h):
    stream = img_to_stream(fig)
    slide.shapes.add_picture(stream, l, t, w, h)
    plt.close(fig)

def footer_bar(slide):
    """Thin accent line at bottom."""
    add_rect(slide, 0, SLIDE_H - Inches(0.06),
             SLIDE_W, Inches(0.06), C_ACCENT)

def slide_label(slide, label: str, number: int):
    """Top-right slide number + section label."""
    add_textbox(slide, f"{label}  |  {number}/9",
                SLIDE_W - Inches(3.2), Inches(0.12), Inches(3.0), Inches(0.35),
                font_size=9, color=C_MID, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)

def section_tag(slide, tag: str):
    """Small coloured pill-style tag top-left."""
    add_rect(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.18), Inches(1.9), Inches(0.28), C_ACCENT)

                Inches(0.35), Inches(0.16), Inches(1.9), Inches(0.30),
                font_size=9, bold=True, color=C_BG, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

def title_block(slide, title, subtitle=None,
                title_size=28, sub_size=16,

    add_textbox(slide, title,
                Inches(0.42), t_offset, width, Inches(0.8),
                font_size=title_size, bold=True, color=C_WHITE)
    if subtitle:
        add_textbox(slide, subtitle,
                    Inches(0.42), t_offset + Inches(0.65), width, Inches(0.5),
                    font_size=sub_size, color=C_MID)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE BUILDERS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def slide_1_title(prs):

    slide = add_slide(prs)

    # gradient-like dark band left
    add_rect(slide, 0, 0, Inches(0.5), SLIDE_H, C_ACCENT)

    # Main title
    add_textbox(slide,
                "Global CO₂ Emissions:",
                Inches(0.85), Inches(1.6), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.9),
                font_size=40, bold=True, color=C_WHITE)
    add_textbox(slide,
                "Who Emits, How Much, and What's Changing",
                Inches(0.85), Inches(2.4), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.9),
                font_size=36, bold=True, color=C_ACCENT)

    # Subtitle / scope
    add_textbox(slide,
                "Fossil Fuels & Industry  ·  1750 – 2024  ·  Policy & Research Edition",
                Inches(0.85), Inches(3.45), Inches(11.0), Inches(0.4),
                font_size=16, color=C_LIGHT)

    # Divider
    add_rect(slide, Inches(0.85), Inches(3.95), Inches(4.5), Inches(0.04), C_ACCENT)

    # Data attribution
    add_textbox(slide,
                "Data: Global Carbon Budget 2025  ·  via Our World in Data\n"
                "Authors: Hannah Ritchie & Max Roser",
                Inches(0.85), Inches(4.1), Inches(9.0), Inches(0.55),
                font_size=12, color=C_MID)

    # Audience tag
    add_textbox(slide,
                "For: Policy Analysts  ·  Climate Negotiators  ·  Sustainability Researchers",
                Inches(0.85), Inches(4.75), Inches(10.0), Inches(0.35),
                font_size=11, italic=True, color=C_MID)

    footer_bar(slide)


def slide_2_global_growth(prs):
    """Line/area chart: 1750-2024 global CO2."""
    slide = add_slide(prs)
    fill_slide_bg(slide, C_BG)
    footer_bar(slide)
    section_tag(slide, "TRAJECTORY")
    slide_label(slide, "Global Growth", 2)

    title_block(slide,
                "Global CO₂ Emissions Grew from 6 Bt in 1950 to Over 35 Bt Today",
                "Fossil-fuel & industry CO₂  |  1750–2024  |  Gt CO₂/yr",
                title_size=24, sub_size=13, t_offset=Inches(0.52))

    # ── Chart ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    years = list(range(1750, 2025, 1))
    def emission_model(y):
        if y < 1800: return 0.008 * (y - 1750)
        if y < 1850: return 0.4 + 0.025 * (y - 1800)
        if y < 1900: return 1.65 + 0.07  * (y - 1850)
        if y < 1950: return 5.15 + 0.018 * (y - 1900)
        if y < 1973: return 6.0  + 0.62  * (y - 1950)
        if y < 1980: return 20.26 - 0.3  * (y - 1973)
        if y < 2000: return 18.16 + 0.42 * (y - 1980)
        if y < 2010: return 26.56 + 0.84 * (y - 2000)
        if y < 2020: return 35.0  + 0.05 * (y - 2010)
        if y < 2023: return 35.5  - 0.15 * (y - 2020)
        return 35.8
    vals = [emission_model(y) for y in years]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, 4.2), facecolor=M_BG)
    ax.set_facecolor(M_BG)
    ax.fill_between(years, vals, alpha=0.25, color=M_ACC)
    ax.plot(years, vals, color=M_ACC, linewidth=2.2)

    # Inflection annotations
    annots = [
        (1950, 6.0,  "1950: 6 Bt",       'right', -30, 30),
        (1990, 22.5, "1990: ~22 Bt",      'left',   15, 15),
        (2010, 35.2, "2010: ~35 Bt",      'left',   12, 20),
        (2024, 35.8, "2024: >35 Bt",      'left',   10, -25),
    ]
    for xv, yv, lbl, ha, dx, dy in annots:
        ax.annotate(lbl, xy=(xv, yv), xytext=(xv+dx, yv+dy),
                    fontsize=9, color=M_LIGHT,
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=M_ACC, lw=1.2),
                    ha=ha)
    # Oil crisis band
    ax.axvspan(1973, 1979, alpha=0.08, color=M_ACC2)
    ax.text(1976, 2, "Oil\nCrisis", ha='center', fontsize=7.5,
            color=M_ACC2, va='bottom')
    # Post-2000 band
    ax.axvspan(2000, 2010, alpha=0.06, color=M_ACC3)
    ax.text(2005, 2, "China\nRise", ha='center', fontsize=7.5,
            color=M_ACC3, va='bottom')

    ax.set_xlim(1750, 2026)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 42)
    ax.set_xlabel("Year", color=M_LIGHT, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel("Gt CO₂ / year", color=M_LIGHT, fontsize=10)
    ax.tick_params(colors=M_MID, labelsize=9)
    ax.spines[:].set_color(M_GRID)
    ax.yaxis.grid(True, color=M_GRID, linewidth=0.6, linestyle='--')
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    fig.tight_layout(pad=0.4)

    add_chart_img(slide, fig, Inches(0.35), Inches(1.65), Inches(9.6), Inches(5.0))

    # Key callout box
    add_rect(slide, Inches(10.15), Inches(1.65), Inches(2.85), Inches(3.6), RGBColor(0x0A, 0x22, 0x38))
    txb = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(10.25), Inches(1.75), Inches(2.65), Inches(3.4))
    txb.word_wrap = True
    tf = txb.text_frame; tf.word_wrap = True
    add_text_para(tf, "Key Inflection Points", font_size=11, bold=True, color=C_ACCENT, space_before=Pt(2))
    add_text_para(tf, "▶  Pre-industrial era: near-zero", font_size=10, color=C_LIGHT, space_before=Pt(6))
    add_text_para(tf, "▶  Post-WWII surge (1950–73)", font_size=10, color=C_LIGHT, space_before=Pt(4))
    add_text_para(tf, "▶  Oil shock pause (1973–79)", font_size=10, color=C_LIGHT, space_before=Pt(4))
    add_text_para(tf, "▶  China-led boom (2000–10)", font_size=10, color=C_LIGHT, space_before=Pt(4))
    add_text_para(tf, "▶  Growth slowing — but NO peak yet", font_size=10, bold=True, color=C_ACCENT2, space_before=Pt(6))


def slide_3_regional_share(prs):
    """Stacked area chart: regional share shift placeholder."""
    slide = add_slide(prs)
    fill_slide_bg(slide, C_BG)
    footer_bar(slide)
    section_tag(slide, "REGIONAL SHIFT")
    slide_label(slide, "Regional Shares", 3)

    title_block(slide,
                "Europe and the US Fell from 90% of Emissions in 1900 to Under One-Third Today",
                "Share of global CO₂ emissions by region  |  1850–2024",
                title_size=22, sub_size=13, t_offset=Inches(0.52))

    # Stacked area chart
    yrs = list(range(1850, 2025, 5))
    def interp(pts, y):
        xs = sorted(pts.keys())
        for i in range(len(xs)-1):
            if xs[i] <= y <= xs[i+1]:
                t = (y - xs[i]) / (xs[i+1] - xs[i])
                return pts[xs[i]] * (1-t) + pts[xs[i+1]] * t
        if y < xs[0]: return pts[xs[0]]
        return pts[xs[-1]]

    # region shares (approximate, consistent with source data)
    eur_pts  = {1850:55, 1900:50, 1950:35, 1970:28, 1990:18, 2010:12, 2024:8}
    usa_pts  = {1850:10, 1900:28, 1950:40, 1970:32, 1990:22, 2010:16, 2024:13}
    chn_pts  = {1850:5,  1900:4,  1950:2,  1970:6,  1990:11, 2010:24, 2024:31}
    ind_pts  = {1850:5,  1900:4,  1950:3,  1970:3,  1990:4,  2010:6,  2024:8}
    oth_pts  = {1850:25, 1900:14, 1950:20, 1970:31, 1990:45, 2010:42, 2024:40}

    eur  = [interp(eur_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    usa  = [interp(usa_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    chn  = [interp(chn_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    ind  = [interp(ind_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    oth  = [interp(oth_pts, y) for y in yrs]

    # Normalize to 100%
    totals = [e+u+c+i+o for e,u,c,i,o in zip(eur,usa,chn,ind,oth)]
    eur  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(eur, totals)]
    usa  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(usa, totals)]
    chn  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(chn, totals)]

def new_prs():
    prs = Presentation()

    prs.slide_height = SLIDE_H
    return prs

def blank_layout(prs):
    return prs.slide_layouts[6]   # completely blank

def add_slide(prs):
    return prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout(prs))

def fill_slide_bg(slide, color: RGBColor):
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_rect(slide, l, t, w, h, fill_color, alpha=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(1, l, t, w, h)   # MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE=1
    shape.line.fill.background()
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    return shape

def add_textbox(slide, text, l, t, w, h,
                font_size=18, bold=False, color=C_WHITE,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, wrap=True, italic=False):
    txb = slide.shapes.add_textbox(l, t, w, h)
    txb.word_wrap = wrap
    tf = txb.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    return txb

def add_text_para(tf, text, font_size=16, bold=False, color=C_LIGHT,
                  align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, space_before=Pt(4), italic=False):
    from pptx.util import Pt as _Pt
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.alignment = align
    p.space_before = space_before
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size = _Pt(font_size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    return p

    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight',
                facecolor=M_BG, edgecolor='none')

    return buf

                return pts[xs[i]] * (1-t) + pts[xs[i+1]] * t

def add_slide(prs):
    return prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout(prs))

def fill_slide_bg(slide, color: RGBColor):
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_rect(slide, l, t, w, h, fill_color, alpha=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(1, l, t, w, h)   # MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE=1
    shape.line.fill.background()
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    return shape

def add_textbox(slide, text, l, t, w, h,
                font_size=18, bold=False, color=C_WHITE,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, wrap=True, italic=False):
    txb = slide.shapes.add_textbox(l, t, w, h)
    txb.word_wrap = wrap
    tf = txb.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    return txb

def add_text_para(tf, text, font_size=16, bold=False, color=C_LIGHT,
                  align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, space_before=Pt(4), italic=False):
    from pptx.util import Pt as _Pt
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.alignment = align
    p.space_before = space_before
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size = _Pt(font_size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    return p

def img_to_stream(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight',
                facecolor=M_BG, edgecolor='none')
    buf.seek(0)
    return buf

def add_chart_img(slide, fig, l, t, w, h):
    stream = img_to_stream(fig)
    slide.shapes.add_picture(stream, l, t, w, h)
    plt.close(fig)

def slide_2_global_growth(prs):
    """Line/area chart: 1750-2024 global CO2."""
    slide = add_slide(prs)
    fill_slide_bg(slide, C_BG)
    footer_bar(slide)
    section_tag(slide, "TRAJECTORY")
    slide_label(slide, "Global Growth", 2)

    title_block(slide,
                "Global CO₂ Emissions Grew from 6 Bt in 1950 to Over 35 Bt Today",
                "Fossil-fuel & industry CO₂  |  1750–2024  |  Gt CO₂/yr",
                title_size=24, sub_size=13, t_offset=Inches(0.52))

    # ── Chart ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    years = list(range(1750, 2025, 1))
    def emission_model(y):
        if y < 1800: return 0.008 * (y - 1750)
        if y < 1850: return 0.4 + 0.025 * (y - 1800)
        if y < 1900: return 1.65 + 0.07  * (y - 1850)
        if y < 1950: return 5.15 + 0.018 * (y - 1900)
        if y < 1973: return 6.0  + 0.62  * (y - 1950)
        if y < 1980: return 20.26 - 0.3  * (y - 1973)
        if y < 2000: return 18.16 + 0.42 * (y - 1980)
        if y < 2010: return 26.56 + 0.84 * (y - 2000)
        if y < 2020: return 35.0  + 0.05 * (y - 2010)
        if y < 2023: return 35.5  - 0.15 * (y - 2020)
        return 35.8
    vals = [emission_model(y) for y in years]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, 4.2), facecolor=M_BG)
    ax.set_facecolor(M_BG)
    ax.fill_between(years, vals, alpha=0.25, color=M_ACC)
    ax.plot(years, vals, color=M_ACC, linewidth=2.2)

    # Inflection annotations
    annots = [
        (1950, 6.0,  "1950: 6 Bt",       'right', -30, 30),
        (1990, 22.5, "1990: ~22 Bt",      'left',   15, 15),
        (2010, 35.2, "2010: ~35 Bt",      'left',   12, 20),
        (2024, 35.8, "2024: >35 Bt",      'left',   10, -25),
    ]
    for xv, yv, lbl, ha, dx, dy in annots:
        ax.annotate(lbl, xy=(xv, yv), xytext=(xv+dx, yv+dy),
                    fontsize=9, color=M_LIGHT,
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=M_ACC, lw=1.2),
                    ha=ha)
    # Oil crisis band
    ax.axvspan(1973, 1979, alpha=0.08, color=M_ACC2)
    ax.text(1976, 2, "Oil\nCrisis", ha='center', fontsize=7.5,
            color=M_ACC2, va='bottom')
    # Post-2000 band
    ax.axvspan(2000, 2010, alpha=0.06, color=M_ACC3)
    ax.text(2005, 2, "China\nRise", ha='center', fontsize=7.5,
            color=M_ACC3, va='bottom')

    ax.set_xlim(1750, 2026)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 42)
    ax.set_xlabel("Year", color=M_LIGHT, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel("Gt CO₂ / year", color=M_LIGHT, fontsize=10)
    ax.tick_params(colors=M_MID, labelsize=9)
    ax.spines[:].set_color(M_GRID)
    ax.yaxis.grid(True, color=M_GRID, linewidth=0.6, linestyle='--')
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    fig.tight_layout(pad=0.4)

    add_chart_img(slide, fig, Inches(0.35), Inches(1.65), Inches(9.6), Inches(5.0))

    # Key callout box
    add_rect(slide, Inches(10.15), Inches(1.65), Inches(2.85), Inches(3.6), RGBColor(0x0A, 0x22, 0x38))
    txb = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(10.25), Inches(1.75), Inches(2.65), Inches(3.4))
    txb.word_wrap = True
    tf = txb.text_frame; tf.word_wrap = True
    add_text_para(tf, "Key Inflection Points", font_size=11, bold=True, color=C_ACCENT, space_before=Pt(2))
    add_text_para(tf, "▶  Pre-industrial era: near-zero", font_size=10, color=C_LIGHT, space_before=Pt(6))

def slide_3_regional_share(prs):
    """Stacked area chart: regional share shift placeholder."""
    slide = add_slide(prs)
    fill_slide_bg(slide, C_BG)
    footer_bar(slide)
    section_tag(slide, "REGIONAL SHIFT")
    slide_label(slide, "Regional Shares", 3)

    title_block(slide,
                "Europe and the US Fell from 90% of Emissions in 1900 to Under One-Third Today",
                "Share of global CO₂ emissions by region  |  1850–2024",
                title_size=22, sub_size=13, t_offset=Inches(0.52))

    # Stacked area chart
    yrs = list(range(1850, 2025, 5))
    def interp(pts, y):
        xs = sorted(pts.keys())
        for i in range(len(xs)-1):
            if xs[i] <= y <= xs[i+1]:
                t = (y - xs[i]) / (xs[i+1] - xs[i])
                return pts[xs[i]] * (1-t) + pts[xs[i+1]] * t
        if y < xs[0]: return pts[xs[0]]
        return pts[xs[-1]]

    # region shares (approximate, consistent with source data)
    eur_pts  = {1850:55, 1900:50, 1950:35, 1970:28, 1990:18, 2010:12, 2024:8}
    usa_pts  = {1850:10, 1900:28, 1950:40, 1970:32, 1990:22, 2010:16, 2024:13}
    chn_pts  = {1850:5,  1900:4,  1950:2,  1970:6,  1990:11, 2010:24, 2024:31}
    ind_pts  = {1850:5,  1900:4,  1950:3,  1970:3,  1990:4,  2010:6,  2024:8}
    oth_pts  = {1850:25, 1900:14, 1950:20, 1970:31, 1990:45, 2010:42, 2024:40}

    eur  = [interp(eur_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    usa  = [interp(usa_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    chn  = [interp(chn_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    ind  = [interp(ind_pts, y) for y in yrs]
    oth  = [interp(oth_pts, y) for y in yrs]

    # Normalize to 100%
    totals = [e+u+c+i+o for e,u,c,i,o in zip(eur,usa,chn,ind,oth)]
    eur  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(eur, totals)]
    usa  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(usa, totals)]
    chn  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(chn, totals)]
    ind  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(ind, totals)]
    oth  = [v/t*100 for v,t in zip(oth, totals)]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, 4.4), facecolor=M_BG)
    ax.set_facecolor(M_BG)

    colors = ['#4FC3F7', '#EF6C00', '#E53935', '#FF8F00', '#546E7A']
    labels = ['Europe', 'United States', 'China', 'India', 'Rest of World']
    data   = [eur, usa, chn, ind, oth]

    ax.stackplot(yrs, data, labels=labels, colors=colors, alpha=0.88)

    # Reference lines
    ax.axvline(1900, color=M_LIGHT, lw=0.8, linestyle=':')
    ax.text(1900.5, 96, "1900:\nEur+US\n>90%", fontsize=7.5, color=M_LIGHT, va='top')
    ax.axvline(1950, color=M_LIGHT, lw=0.8, linestyle=':')
    ax.text(1950.5, 96, "1950:\nEur+US\n>85%", fontsize=7.5, color=M_LIGHT, va='top')
    ax.axvline(2024, color=M_ACC, lw=1.2, linestyle='--')
    ax.text(2022, 50, "2024:\nEur+US\n<⅓", fontsize=7.5, color=M_ACC, va='center', ha='right')

    ax.set_xlim(1850, 2024)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
    ax.set_xlabel("Year", color=M_LIGHT, fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel("Share of Global CO₂ (%)", color=M_LIGHT, fontsize=10)
    ax.tick_params(colors=M_MID, labelsize=9)
    ax.spines[:].set_color(M_GRID)
    ax.yaxis.grid(True, color=M_GRID, linewidth=0.5, linestyle='--')
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    leg = ax.legend(loc='lower left', fontsize=8, framealpha=0.25,
                    labelcolor=M_LIGHT, facecolor=M_BG, edgecolor=M_GRID)
    fig.tight_layout(pad=0.4)

    add_chart_img(slide, fig, Inches(0.35), Inches(1.65), Inches(9.7), Inches(5.1))

    # Side callout
    add_rect(slide, Inches(10.2), Inches(1.65), Inches(2.8), Inches(3.0), RGBColor(0x0A, 0x22, 0x38))
    txb = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(10.3), Inches(1.75), Inches(2.6), Inches(2.85))
    txb.word_wrap = True
    tf = txb.text_frame; tf.word_wrap = True
    add_text_para(tf, "The Historic Inversion", font_size=11, bold=True, color=C_ACCENT, space_before=Pt(2))
    add_text_para(tf, "1900  Eur + US > 90%", font_size=10, color=C_LIGHT, space_before=Pt(6))
    add_text_para(tf, "1950  Eur + US > 85%", font_size=10, color=C_LIGHT, space_before=Pt(4))

    footer_bar(slide)

                font_size=26, bold=True, color=C_WHITE)

    # Sub-label
    add_textbox(slide,
                "Global Carbon Budget 2025  ·  Our World in Data  ·  Fossil Fuels & Industry 1750–2024",
                Inches(0.45), Inches(1.1), Inches(10.0), Inches(0.3),
                font_size=10, color=C_MID)

    takeaways = [
        (
            "01  No peak yet",
            "Global CO₂ from fossil fuels exceeds 35 Bt/yr and continues to rise — the world has not yet reached peak emissions despite slowing growth.",

            "Europe and the US dominated emissions throughout the 20th century (>90% in 1900, >85% in 1950). The cumulative atmospheric stock of CO₂ reflects this legacy.",

    # Source note
    add_textbox(slide,
                "Source: Global Carbon Budget 2025 via Our World in Data  ·  ourworldindata.org/co2-emissions",
